span.label: Goal match enhancement appeared only at contacts in the left posterior hippocampus, whereas perceptual mismatch enhancement appeared bilaterally across both anterior and posterior hippocampus.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The perceptual mismatch signal began before the goal match signal in every one of the eight participants.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The two hippocampal signals divide by content: match enhancement tracks the match to the maintained goal while mismatch enhancement tracks perceptual mismatch, dissociating components of working memory within the hippocampus.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Participants whose right posterior hippocampus produced a later perceptual mismatch enhancement were more accurate, a positive correlation between latency and memory performance.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: That latency-accuracy link is read as evidence that the right posterior hippocampal mismatch latency indexes the quality of memory retrieval.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In six of the eight patients, single-trial intracranial field potentials from the right hippocampus were sufficient to classify whether the trial was a match task or a switch task.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Behaviourally, responses were faster in the match task than in the switch task.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Hippocampal engagement here is attributed to the task requiring object identity and location to be bound together, in both the match and the switch task.
